impact.formula: Tagrisso US 2025 = $3,064m, +$301m (20-F p.26); H1 2026 US $1,579m, +10% (interim report p.38). J&J Rybrevant/Lazcluze US 2025 = $534m, +$277m, all lines including exon 20 and second line (JNJ 10-K p.83); worldwide H1 2026 $546m, +70% (JNJ 10-Q p.33). J&J's US franchise is 17% of Tagrisso US and added fewer dollars in 2025. Sensitivity only: each 5% of Tagrisso US sales lost to the J&J regimen = 3,064 x 5% = $153m revenue (assumption), EPS 153 x 0.8 / 1,550 = $0.08. Base = $0 measured erosion to date (Tagrisso US still growing), bear = $153m (5% shift by 2027, assumption, for example if subcutaneous Rybrevant Faspro, named in the JNJ 10-K, removes the infusion burden), bull = $0.

peer.note: Rival is J&J Rybrevant plus Lazcluze (the case's named Tagrisso competitor). Lazcluze 2024 Part D: 183 beneficiaries, $7.1m (partial launch year) vs Tagrisso 12,370 beneficiaries, $1,627m (CMS Part D DY2024 files in data/corpus/drugs/).

confidence_reason: Sales and label figures are verified; drug-label quotes are grep-checked because label files have no page markers. Rybrevant US sales include non-first-line use, so the comparison overstates J&J's first-line base; the impact is a sensitivity.
mechanism: First-line EGFR patients started on Rybrevant plus Lazcluze do not take Tagrisso, so each shift cuts Tagrisso US volume; the label burden slows that shift, which is why Tagrisso US still grows.
part2_hook: Defend Tagrisso with Tagrisso plus chemotherapy (FLAURA2) where an OS benefit is wanted, rather than conceding the OS argument to the J&J regimen.
open_question: First-line share split between osimertinib alone, FLAURA2 and MARIPOSA regimens; Rybrevant Faspro uptake.
